title: The torsion stratum bound
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. All schemes and scheme morphisms below are in the separated finite-type $k$-scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$, and a uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $\mathcal O_{E,Y}=p_Y^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. A lisse lattice means a module sheaf locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{E,Y}^{\oplus r}$ for a finite $r\ge0$ in the pro-étale topology. For a lattice $L_0$ on $Y$, its dual is $L_0^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_{E,Y}}(L_0,\mathcal O_{E,Y})$. For a locally closed immersion $b:T\hookrightarrow X$, write $b=k_b\circ v_b$ with $v_b:T\hookrightarrow B$ open and $k_b:B\hookrightarrow X$ closed, and use $b_!=k_{b,*}v_{b,!}$, the closed direct image after open extension by zero [def-sfb-module-lower-star, def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. Cohomological dimensions have the extended nonnegative-integer convention of [sk-def-cd]; if an upper endpoint is $+\infty$, its cohomological upper bound imposes no condition.

Let $a=i\circ u\colon S\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $i$ closed, $u$ open, and let
$j\colon X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ be the open complement of $Z$. Let $L_0$ be a lisse
$\mathcal O_{E,S}$-module (finite free locally), $b\colon T\hookrightarrow X$ locally closed and $M_0$ a
lisse $\mathcal O_{E,T}$-lattice. Then for every $n\geq1$:

1. $R\underline\Gamma_Z\,b_!(M_0/\pi_E^n)$ lies in
   $\D^{[0,\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+1]}(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)$, with cohomology sheaves
   pulled back from $Z_{\mathrm{ét}}$;
2. $H^qR\Gamma\bigl(S,(L_0^\vee/\pi_E^n)\otimes u^*R\underline\Gamma_Z\,b_!(M_0/\pi_E^n)\bigr)=0$ for
   $q>\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+1$.

proof.text:
Fix $n\ge1$ and put $A=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$. The coefficient definition [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] makes $A$ a finite ring. Since $|\ell|_E<1$, the same definition gives $\ell\in(\pi_E)$ and hence $\ell^n A=0$. Clause (1) of [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients] identifies $\mathcal O_{E,Y}/\pi_E^n$ with the constant ring sheaf $A_Y$. On a cover trivializing a lattice, its reduction is therefore $A_Y^{\oplus r}$; the dual lattice has the dual free basis, so its reduction has the same property. The standing schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since the spectrum of a field is Noetherian. In particular, the open subschemes $S$ of $Z$ and $V=X\setminus Z$ of $X$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], their underlying spaces satisfy the descending chain condition on closed subsets. An open cover with no finite subcover would produce a strictly increasing sequence of finite unions of its members, contradicting that condition on their complements. These schemes are qcqs: their quasi-compactness is part of Noetherianity, and intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact because a Noetherian topological space has all opens quasi-compact. For $j:V\hookrightarrow X$, the inverse image of an affine open is such an open and is quasi-compact; its diagonal is an isomorphism, so $j$ is qcqs. The closed immersion $k_b$ is affine, by the affine quotient description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], and is qcqs for the same reason applied to its affine inverse images and its isomorphism diagonal. Use the small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. For each such ringed site, [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] makes its module-sheaf category Grothendieck abelian, hence it has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. We also fix how these bounds are read on underlying abelian sheaves, as required by [sk-def-cd]. Write $U_Y$ for forgetting the $A_Y$-action. This is the direct image for the identity topos with ring map $\mathbf Z_Y\to A_Y$, and is exact because kernels and cokernels are computed on underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The two factorizations of the ringed morphism $(V,A_V)\to(X,\mathbf Z_X)$, and separately the factorization $(S,A_S)\to(S,\mathbf Z_S)\to(*,\mathbf Z)$, give by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]
$$U_XRj_{*,A}\cong Rj_{*,\mathbf Z}U_V,\qquad R\Gamma_{A}(S,-)\cong R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}(S,U_S-).$$
Here $R\Gamma_A$ takes values in abelian groups, and $RU_Y=U_Y$ by exactness. Thus the derived direct-image and section bounds in the coefficient category are exactly the underlying abelian bounds in the cd definition.

source.place: Opening paragraph: finite reductions and the qcqs hypotheses required by the two site comparisons

proof.text:
Put $F_n=M_0/\pi_E^n$. Step 1 shows that $F_n$ is locally constant with finite $A$-module stalks. Apply [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] on $T$ to obtain a lisse etale sheaf $F_n^{\mathrm{et}}$ with $
u_T^*F_n^{\mathrm{et}}\cong F_n$. Use the factorization $b=k_bv_b$ in the statement. By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], $v_{b,!}F_n\cong
u_B^*v_{b,!}^{\mathrm{et}}F_n^{\mathrm{et}}$. Apply [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] to the qcqs map $k_b$ and take degree-zero cohomology. Inverse image for comparison is exact by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules], and $H^0Rk_{b,*}$ on a sheaf is ordinary $k_{b,*}$ by [lem-sp-derived-well-defined] (the module categories have enough injectives by step 1), so
$$N:=b_!F_n=k_{b,*}v_{b,!}F_n\cong
u_X^* igl(k_{b,*}^{\mathrm{et}}v_{b,!}^{\mathrm{et}}F_n^{\mathrm{et}} igr).$$
Thus $N$ is a classical sheaf of $A$-modules.

source.place: Opening paragraph: descent of the lisse reduction, open extension and closed direct image

proof.text:
Write $N=\nu_X^*N^{\mathrm{et}}$ using step 2. The inverse-image square in [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] gives $j^*N=\nu_V^*j_{\mathrm{et}}^*N^{\mathrm{et}}$. Since $j$ is qcqs by step 1, the same theorem gives
$$B_j:=Rj_*j^*N\cong\nu_X^*Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}j_{\mathrm{et}}^*N^{\mathrm{et}}.$$
Consequently its cohomology sheaves are classical. It has no negative cohomology: using enough injectives from step 1, embed $j^*N$ in an injective $I^0$, then successively embed each cokernel in $I^1,I^2,\ldots$. This gives an injective resolution in nonnegative degrees, and [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective](2) computes $B_j$ by applying $j_*$ to that resolution. By [sk-def-cd], applied to the classical $\ell$-power torsion sheaf $j^*N$, $H^r(B_j)=0$ for $r>c:=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)$. The coefficient $A$ is admissible and $X$ is a standing scheme, so the hypotheses of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support](1) hold and give
$$R\underline\Gamma_ZN=i^*C,\qquad C=\operatorname{fib}(N\longrightarrow B_j).$$

source.place: Paragraph (1): restriction, comparison for Rj_*, cohomological dimension, and the support fiber formula

proof.text:
The long exact sequence of $C\to N\to B_j\to C[1]$ from [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives $H^r(C)=0$ for $r<0$,
$$H^0(C)=\ker(N\to H^0B_j),\quad H^1(C)=\operatorname{coker}(N\to H^0B_j),\quad H^r(C)\cong H^{r-1}(B_j)\ (r\ge2).$$
Every displayed sheaf is classical: [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] says comparison is exact and fully faithful, so the map between classical sheaves lifts to an etale map, whose kernel and cokernel pull back to these two sheaves. For finite $c$, the formulas give vanishing above $c+1$; for $c=+\infty$ only the proved lower bound is required. By [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image], $i^*$ is exact, and the inverse-image square of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] identifies $i^*\nu_X^*$ with $\nu_Z^*i_{\mathrm{et}}^*$. Thus applying $i^*$ preserves the bounds and etale origin, proving assertion (1).

source.place: Paragraph (1): explicit long exact sequence and preservation of etale origin

proof.text:
Put $P_n=L_0^\vee/\pi_E^n$ and $G=P_n\otimes_Au^*R\underline\Gamma_ZN$. By step 1, $P_n$ is finite locally free over $A_S$. The tensor clause of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support-ii] computes this functor by ordinary termwise tensor; locally it is a finite direct sum, hence exact. Exactness of $u^*$ [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] gives
$$H^v(G)=P_n\otimes_Au^*H^v(R\underline\Gamma_ZN),$$
zero outside $[0,c+1]$ when $c$ is finite. The inverse-image square in [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] makes the second tensor factor classical. Also $P_n=
u_S^*P_n^{\mathrm{et}}$ by [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin]. To check tensor descent, trivialize the locally constant $P_n^{\mathrm{et}}$ on an etale cover, with value a finite $A$-module $Q$. This module has a finite presentation $A^r	o A^s	o Q	o0$ since $A$ is finite. For a classical sheaf $
u_S^*H$, $Q\otimes_A
u_S^*H$ is the cokernel of the corresponding matrix map $(
u_S^*H)^r	o(
u_S^*H)^s$ by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Exact comparison [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] identifies this with the pullback of $Q\otimes_A H$. These identifications send each pure tensor to the same pure tensor, so agree on overlaps and glue to $P_n\otimes_A
u_S^*H\cong
u_S^*(P_n^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_AH)$. Every $H^v(G)$ is therefore classical and is killed by $\ell^n$.

source.place: Paragraph (2): exact finite-free tensor and classical cohomology

proof.text:
Let $d=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)$. If $c$ or $d$ is $+\infty$, no integer $q$ exceeds $c+d+1$, so assertion (2) is vacuous. Otherwise step 5 puts $G$ in the finite interval $[0,c+1]$. Use the small-site universe convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], the category of $A_S$-module sheaves is Grothendieck abelian; the target category of abelian groups is the same construction on the punctual site with ring $\mathbf Z$. Global sections is additive and left exact, since evaluation preserves kernels. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to this global-sections functor and a bounded-below representative of $G$, with lower bound $0$. Its page and convergence clauses give
$$E_2^{p,v}=H^p(S,H^v(G))\Longrightarrow H^{p+v}R\Gamma(S,G),$$
with a finite exhaustive separated filtration in each total degree. By [sk-def-cd] and step 5, $E_2^{p,v}=0$ for $p>d$, and it is zero unless $0\le v\le c+1$. For a total degree $q>c+d+1$, either $v>c+1$ or $p=q-v>d$, so every $E_2$ term on that diagonal is zero. Every subsequent term and hence every $E_\infty$ term on the diagonal is zero. All graded pieces of the finite abutment filtration vanish, so $H^qR\Gamma(S,G)=0$, proving assertion (2).
